subject.title: fix(cron): detect ===DONE_ERR=== sentinel in agent final text as failure signal

question: Should `===DONE_ERR===` in an agent-visible final response be a supported durable cron-failure protocol, or must failure be emitted only by an explicit structured execution outcome?
rationale: The patch intentionally changes persistent scheduler state and alerting semantics from model-visible text; code review cannot determine whether that implicit protocol is an accepted product contract.

options.title: Require structured terminal outcomes
options.body: Keep visible text informational and add a producer-owned structured terminal failure result from the execution path that can authoritatively report failure.

options.title: Adopt the sentinel contract explicitly
options.body: Accept terminal sentinel parsing as a public cron contract, document its collision semantics, and add end-to-end upgrade coverage for status, accounting, and alerts.

recommendation.title: Require structured terminal outcomes
recommendation.body: Keep visible text informational and add a producer-owned structured terminal failure result from the execution path that can authoritatively report failure.

likelyOwner.reason: The central owner must be established from the embedded-agent and cron feature history before selecting the durable failure contract.
